posts.title: Every flight in America is grounded. The FAA halted all departures after a telecom outage #209audit
posts.caption: Merced County spending. Administrative accountability. Every flight in America is grounded. The FAA halted all departures after a telecom outage hit the centers that guide planes between airports. About 3,100 planes were already in the air when the stop began, just before one in the afternoon. Fresno took a diverted flight, and Merced's only airline, Contour, flies to Los Angeles and Las Vegas, grounded too. Delays climbed past 8,000, with more than 400 cancellations. The last nationwide ground stop was January 2023. Check before you fly. Full story in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio. #FAA #GroundStop #CentralValley #MercedCounty

posts.title: Randy Villegas defeats David Valadao in CA-22 — AP tally 95,831 to 45,344
posts.caption: Central Valley governance. Merced County spending. Administrative accountability. A professor flipped a six-term seat. Randy Villegas beat David Valadao in California's 22nd district, 95,831 to 45,344 on the AP tally. The race turned on Medicaid and the cost of living, and on an immigration-enforcement gap voters could see in their own Valley. What does a new generation do with the job now? Full breakdown in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: UC Merced 1300 Campaign: 1,300 young men of color into UC and CSU by 2026
posts.caption: Central Valley governance. Merced County spending. Administrative accountability. UC Merced is measuring itself on who it lifts, not who it leaves behind. Today the 1300 Campaign gathers on campus to check the count: 1,300 young men of color into the UC and CSU systems by 2026. Chancellor Juan Sanchez Munoz opens the summit, partners review the data, the trends, and the plan for the coming year. A campaign that names a number and publishes the count is a campaign that can be held to account. Watch the count. Full story in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: California Passed the Right Reading Law. Then It Walked Away.
posts.caption:
Central Valley governance. Merced County spending. Administrative accountability.

California adopted the science of reading, the most cost-effective way to raise achievement. Then it gave districts 31 training programs to choose from, or they could pick their own, or skip training entirely. $500M went to literacy coaches, and many districts never hired one. Mississippi did the opposite: one program, every teacher, every administrator. A policy with 31 options and no owner is not a policy. It is a suggestion.

Full record in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

- Source: EdSource (Nov 13, 2026)

posts.title: VANCE OFF IRAN. CALIFORNIA NAMED.
posts.caption: Trump just pulled JD Vance off the Iran file. The vice president spent months leading the diplomacy himself, and now he has been ordered to turn his full attention to Democratic-run cities and states, with California named by name. The blockade in the Strait of Hormuz stays in place, and Iran says a tanker hit a naval mine today. Here is the systems question: when the diplomat becomes the enforcer, the negotiation does not pause, it ends. And the target list is not overseas anymore. It is domestic. California, Minnesota, Illinois. That is the shift to watch. Full record in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio. - Just Security, Nov 13

posts.title: Becerra's Next Test: Childcare in the Central Valley
posts.caption: Central Valley governance. Merced County spending. Administrative accountability. Governor-elect Becerra just named childcare as his next test, and the budget is the receipt. In the Central Valley that promise lands hard: a childcare bill can swallow a paycheck and one closed classroom can cost a parent a shift. He has 55 days to staff a government and write a budget against an $18.5B deficit. Will improved childcare mean more slots, lower costs, and better pay for providers, or just a line in a speech? Watch the budget, not the press release. Deep dives every Tuesday in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio, free.

posts.title: Federal judge orders release of man ICE re-detained; Pomona reports pre-dawn arrest Nov. 12
posts.caption:
A federal judge ordered him free on November 10. The government did not even oppose it.

ICE had taken him back on October 27, after a judge had already ordered his release.

In Denver, the acting field office director testified he ordered agents to re-arrest people judges had freed. At least 18 people were taken back. A judge there is weighing contempt.

And on November 12, a community alert reported ICE taking one person from an Arco station in Pomona at about 5:40 a.m. That report is still unverified. Two more sightings in Claremont and Ontario the same morning are unverified too.

But the pattern is verified: a court orders release, and the agency takes them back anyway.

If a federal judge's release order does not stop a re-arrest, what does?

Full record in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.
- The Pomonan

posts.caption: Central Valley classrooms are emptying, and it is not birth rates doing it. A Stanford study found absences spiked more than 20 percent in Valley communities hit by ICE raids. One teacher counted 200 students gone on day one. The record is public. Full breakdown in the 209connect newsletter. - Source: Stanford study

posts.title: The $75 Billion Trade: Jeffries Draws the Line on ICE Funding
posts.caption: Central Valley public audit | Merced County governance | administrative due process. Jeffries is offering a trade, not just a no. House Democrats will not fund what he calls a violent mass deportation machine, and $75 billion is already set aside for ICE through 2029. The systems question is what that money buys versus what a deal buys: bipartisan action this year on the Dream and Promise Act, a path to permanent residence for people who came here as kids and for people who lost protected status. The deadline is January, when the new Congress takes over. Funding fight or deal? That is the choice coming. Source: USA Today, Nov 9, 2026. Follow 209connect for the record behind the headline.

posts.title: The water isn't coming back.
posts.caption: The water isn't coming back. A new study in Water Resources Research tracked 65 specialty crops county by county. Half the groundwater growing America's fruits, nuts, and vegetables is pumped faster than aquifers refill. In the Central Valley, more than 9 in 10 drops of specialty-crop irrigation come from that same overdraft. Almonds took more than 1 in 4 of those drops. The Valley feeds the country on water it can't replace. Full breakdown in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio. - Water Resources Research

posts.title: Newsom announces $1.3B for cleaner transit; Merced County to expand zero-emission microtransit
posts.caption:
Merced County is getting cleaner rides.

Governor Newsom announced nearly $1.3 billion for cleaner transit across California, and Merced County is expanding zero-emission microtransit. Smaller clean vehicles, reaching the neighborhoods big buses don't.

The funding also modernizes transit facilities and puts battery-electric buses on the road in Kings County. Cleaner air, better connections, and the Valley is part of it.

Full breakdown in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio. - Governor's Office

posts.title: New ICE detention facility opens in Appleton, Minnesota: 1,600 beds, $495.6 million
posts.caption:
Half a billion. 1,600 beds.

A new ICE detention facility opened this week in Appleton, Minnesota. DHS says it opened November 9. The site is the former Prairie Correctional Facility, a private prison empty since 2010, bought for $495.6 million. Full operation is expected by mid-2027.

It sits in the Eighth Circuit, where a federal appeals court has already approved holding many immigrants without bond.

Full record in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

- Source: MPR News / Fox 9

posts.title: LAUSD locks in $100M a year for Black Student Achievement Plan
posts.caption:
100M a year. Locked in.

LAUSD just voted to fund its Black Student Achievement Plan at $100M a year for the next two school years, above the $75M first proposed, while projecting a $3.6B shortfall the year after next. A federal probe into the program is still open.

When a board wants to fund something, the money appears. Follow the line items, not the press release. Read the full record in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

- Source: NY Post
